Data alone is never enough to generalize -- every learner must embody some assumptions or knowledge beyond the data it's given in order to generalize beyond it.

testCases.expectedOutput: Model ensembles (bagging, boosting, stacking) change the hypothesis space itself, e.g. from single decision trees to linear combinations of them. BMA instead assigns fixed-formula weights to hypotheses within the original space, and those weights are so skewed toward the single highest-weight classifier that BMA becomes nearly equivalent to just picking that one classifier. Domingos concludes model ensembles are a key part of the ML toolkit, while BMA is seldom worth the trouble.
